items.title: Trump says agreement with Iran over end of war is 'largely negotiated'
items.description: US President Donald Trump ​says a memorandum of understanding ​on ‌a peace deal with Iran that would open the Strait of Hormuz has been "largely negotiated", with ‌details ​to ‌be unveiled soon.

items.title: Labor's tax defence is backfiring with young voters
items.description: Labor is banking on younger generations, who are overwhelmingly wage earners, being more interested in owning their own home than pocketing higher profits on a lucky crypto trade.

items.title: The scale of the mouse plague is hard to fathom. Here's a visualisation
items.description: A mouse plague is invading farms and homes in southern and Western Australia. But what does that really look like?

items.title: Former actor Rachel Ward became a farmhand at 65 and found her purpose
items.description: With the country wind in her grey hair, cow dung on her boots and not a skerrick of make-up, former actor Rachel Ward has found her place, sharing her passion for regenerative farming.

items.title: 'Not a fringe hobby for inner-city weirdos': What's blocking bikes in cities?
items.description: Climate change, the cost-of-living crisis and healthy lifestyle goals should make active transport like cycling a no brainer. So why does Australia struggle to build a bike culture?

items.title: 'An absolutely pleasant surprise': Why single mums are moving in together
items.description: As rental and living costs surge, and as single mums remain one of the most vulnerable groups in the country, some are moving in together and finding many benefits.

items.title: 'I've had enough': Why this loyal Labor voter is switching to One Nation
items.description: The next opportunity to test support for One Nation in Western Sydney will be the state election on March 13. Already, disillusioned Labor voter Silvana Rota is ready to "give them a go".

items.title: Maldives cave dive deaths leave us with many theories and one big question
items.description: The question of why experienced divers would descend to depths of more than 50 metres on a single tank of air — let alone enter a cave while doing so — baffles members of the relatively close-knit deep-sea diving community.

items.title: Five economists share opinions on Labor's budget and Coalition's reply
items.description: Five leading economists weigh in on the budget and reply debate, embracing many of the ideas raised while also arguing that "bigger tax reform is needed."

items.title: This private island paradise has a bargain price tag, and problems galore
items.description: Makri Island, not far from mainland Greece, boasts almost 100 hectares of uninhabited Mediterranean beauty, but buyers be warned, this slice of paradise comes with a catch.

items.title: When a phantom killed Dawn Hillier, he returned the knife to her kitchen and vanished
items.description: Teenage Dawn Hillier was a "ray of sunshine". Almost 50 years later, years of investigation, a coronial inquiry, and a big reward have been unable to solve her brutal murder.

items.title: Multiple safety violations in China mine explosion, investigation finds
items.description: An explosion at a coal mine in China that killed at least 82 people was the result of the company involved having committed multiple serious safety violations, an early investigation has found.

items.title: Auckland makes A-League history with grand-final triumph over Sydney
items.description: Auckland has become the first side from New Zealand to win an A-League Men championship after downing competition heavyweight Sydney 1-0 in a cagey season decider.

items.title: Jamie-Lee Price thinks fake tan could solve a lot of netball's problems
items.description: Frustrated at netball's stagnation, this is what Jamie-Lee Price wants to see happen to keep her sport moving with the times.

items.title: Meet the women turning bicycle tyres and timber offcuts into furniture
items.description: These artists are carving out a niche in a traditionally male space, using recycled materials and offcuts to create beautiful furniture, and even making music to accompany the work.

items.title: Put away the dictionary. It's spelling bee time!
items.description: Know your way around a homonym? Nah, me neither but come in and have a crack at our Sunday quiz anyway.

items.title: As a kid, Thitiwoot wanted to name a dino. He never knew it'd be this big
items.description: It started out as a bone sticking out of the mud next to a lake in Thailand — and now scientists say it's the biggest dinosaur ever found in South-East Asia.

items.title: Trump revives centuries-old doctrine that shaped US-Cuba relations
items.description: The Monroe Doctrine was once a core tenet of US foreign policy. US President Donald Trump has brought it back with a new interpretation.

items.title: Mystery billboard bites back at critics of Olympic rowing location
items.description: Amid months of debate about the location for the 2032 Olympic rowing events, a billboard came to life. Who put it there and why was a mystery until now.

items.title: 'There's more in the tank:' Pendlebury celebrates games record despite Eagles scare
items.description: Collingwood's No.10 enjoys a 10-point win in his record-breaking match as the Magpies hold firm to down the Eagles at the MCG.

items.title: 'Stay with us': Dragons booed off the field at home ahead of fan day
items.description: St George Illawarra is 0-11 to start the 2026 season after losing to the Warriors in Kogarah, while the Sea Eagles continue their strong form with a hard-fought victory over Gold Coast.

items.title: Iran war lays bare overlooked holes in Australia's sovereign capability
items.description: The Iran war has not only highlighted the vulnerability of global supply chains — it has also exposed the overlooked parts of Australia's manufacturing sector needed in a crisis.

items.title: Man allegedly armed with gun shot dead by police north of Brisbane
items.description: Queensland Police said the man approached officers and made threats towards police whilst armed with a firearm, and as a result was shot.

items.title: From farm gate to stage door, theatre is a release from life on the land
items.description: Putting their livestock, tractors and drought feeding aside for a night, these farmers are taking to the stage.

items.title: Socceroos duo's Premier League dream dashed as Hull beat Middlesbrough
items.description: Middlesbrough's two Socceroos, Riley McGree and Sammy Silvera, have been left shattered after all the drama surrounding the Championship play-offs ended with a deflating, last-gasp 1-0 defeat to Premier League-bound Hull City at Wembley.
